source: Krenn & Zeilinger (2020) Predicting research trends with semantic and neural networks with an application in quantum physics (PNAS)
finding: Built SEMNET, a concept network from paper abstracts (6368 quantum-physics concepts; link = two concepts in one abstract). A small neural net on 17 network features ranks unlinked pairs by chance of being linked within 5 years.
numbers: AUC 0.85 for the 2017 test (trained on data to 2012). Features: degrees, paper counts, cosine similarity, path counts of length 2-4, distances. Restricted to pairs sharing under 20% of neighbours. Roughly 5% of possible edges drawn by end of 2017.
limits: One field (quantum physics). Co-occurrence of terms, not a claim that the idea is good. Pairs sharing many neighbours excluded to avoid synonyms.
agent_relevance: Gap-finding in a concept graph is predictable from structure alone. An agent memory could rank 'unlinked but structurally close' concept pairs as candidate analogies to retrieve.

source: Krenn, Buffoni, Coutinho, et al. (2022/2023) Forecasting the future of AI with machine learning-based link prediction in an exponentially growing knowledge network (Nature Machine Intelligence)
finding: Science4Cast benchmark: a semantic network of AI literature (about 64,000 concept nodes) and ten methods to predict new links. Hand-crafted network features beat methods that learn features themselves.
numbers: Best AUC up to 93% for predicting one new link; links that appear at least 3 times predicted with AUC about 99.5%. Arxiv AI papers double about every 23 months. Clustering coefficient fell 0.919 (1999) to 0.650 (2013); network grows more centralised.
limits: Authors ran leakage and duplication checks. Quasi-deterministic result for triple links is unexplained. Pure ML did not beat feature-based models at the time.
agent_relevance: Simple structural features (neighbour counts, PageRank, Jaccard) are a strong, cheap baseline for 'which pair of ideas will connect'. Good to code-check, no model call needed.

source: Gu & Krenn (2024-2026, v4) Generating Interesting Scientific Ideas using Knowledge Graphs and LLMs (SciMuse)
finding: Knowledge graph of 58 million papers plus an LLM generated personalised research ideas. More than 100 group leaders rated 4,451 ideas. Picking concept pairs with the graph did NOT beat a titles-only GPT baseline.
numbers: Mean interest 2.40 of 5; most common rating 1; 24.9% rated 4 or 5 (394 rated 5, 713 rated 4). By condition: 2.350 (high-citation-predicted pairs), 2.446 (random pairs), 2.414 (titles-only GPT). 110 evaluators.
limits: Ratings are interest, not truth or later impact. Graph pair selection tuned for predicted citations, not for interest.
agent_relevance: Graph-picked concept pairs add no measured value for idea quality by themselves. Do not assume a knowledge graph improves ideas; test against a plain baseline.

source: Gu & Krenn (2026) SciMuse, graph features versus interest
finding: The better connected and more cited a concept is, the less interesting the resulting idea. Distance between the evaluator's field and the idea also lowers interest.
numbers: Binned slopes: degree -0.213 (idea-level Spearman -0.166); PageRank -0.192 (rho -0.176); citations last year -0.162 (rho -0.143); total citations -0.143 (rho -0.153); semantic distance researcher-to-idea -0.309 (R2 0.734, rho -0.223). N = 2,996 suggestions.
limits: Correlations are small at idea level. Rater pool is Max Planck group leaders.
agent_relevance: Popular hubs give obvious ideas; far-away ideas feel irrelevant. Retrieval should aim at mid-distance, lower-degree nodes, near the asker's own context.

source: Gu & Krenn (2026) SciMuse, predicting interest
finding: Interest can be predicted weakly. A supervised network on graph features and a zero-shot LLM pairwise ranker both beat chance; the LLM did best.
numbers: AUC 63.20 +/- 0.31% (neural net), 67.44 +/- 0.01% (GPT-4o), 60.39 +/- 0.02% (third method, as listed in paper). Task: ideas rated 4-5 versus 3 or below.
limits: Weak predictors. Trained on one rater pool.
agent_relevance: An LLM comparing two candidate ideas pairwise against the user's context is a usable but weak filter; combine with code-side checks.

source: Gu & Krenn (2026) SciMuse, human versus LLM ideas
finding: Ideas written by PhD students and ideas from GPT-4 and GPT-5.2 got similar interest ratings from the same six evaluators.
limits: Small, six evaluators, physics-related fields only.
agent_relevance: Newer models are no worse than trained juniors on perceived interest; the gain from the model is bigger than the gain from graph retrieval.

source: Sourati & Evans (2023) Accelerating science with human-aware artificial intelligence (Nature Human Behaviour)
finding: Added the people who write papers to the knowledge network. Models that know scientist behaviour predict discoveries better; models that avoid human-likely paths find complementary hypotheses.
numbers: Up to 400% better precision on predicting future discoveries; about 100% precision gain for materials properties; 43% higher precision than content-only in one test; drug-repurposing trial predictions 36-38% precision then 42% (vs 10-12% for content-only); materials precision 62/58/74% with authors vs 48/50/58% without (thermoelectric/ferroelectric/photovoltaic).
limits: Predicts what humans will find, not what is true. Retrospective tests.
agent_relevance: The link graph should model who or what usually connects ideas. An agent can deliberately choose pairs humans rarely join, to reduce shared blind spots (links to G-guardrails on correlated errors).

source: Sourati & Evans (2023) discovery wait times
finding: Discoveries that models rank as unlikely for human experts take longer to occur; wait time grows as the method steers away from human-reachable paths.
numbers: Average wait times rise as the avoidance parameter increases across human diseases and materials; reported in Fig. 6 (no single headline number).
limits: Exact values only in figures.
agent_relevance: Out-of-pattern links are slower to confirm; budget extra verification for them.

source: Wang, Downey, Ji, Hope (2023/2024) SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty (ACL 2024)
finding: Retrieves 'inspirations' from a literature knowledge graph (semantic, KG-neighbour and citation neighbours) and iteratively rewrites ideas until they are not too similar to prior papers. GPT-4 alone gives low technical depth and novelty.
numbers: Human study: in 85% of comparisons the real paper idea beat the best model idea on technical level and novelty. First novelty iteration made about 56% of ideas more novel; second raised novelty for 57.8% of those that continued; novelty never dropped. Preprocessing extraction precision 91-100% except relation extraction 65%; 79.7% of instances passed all steps.
limits: Generated ideas still far below the true ones. Extraction noise. Models tend to copy retrieved text.
agent_relevance: A retrieve-then-compare-to-prior loop (novelty check against retrieved neighbours) is a code-checkable operator. Add a copy penalty.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review: LLM ideas (retrieval over papers, then generation and ranking) were judged more novel than human expert ideas but slightly less feasible.
numbers: Novelty mean 5.64 (AI) vs 4.84 (human), p<0.05 (p<0.01 in one test); N=49 ideas per condition, 79 reviewers, 298 reviews, 104 participants. Of 4,000 seed ideas only about 200 (about 5%) were non-duplicates (similarity cutoff 0.8). LLM ranker accuracy 71.4% (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) on ICLR accept/reject pairs.
limits: Only NLP prompting topic; novelty judged before execution; LLM self-evaluation failed; diversity collapses.
agent_relevance: Generation without diversity control wastes budget: 95% duplicates. Count and dedupe in code; do not trust the model to rank its own ideas.

source: Gutierrez, Shu, Gu, Yasunaga, Su (2024) HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for LLMs (NeurIPS 2024)
finding: Builds a knowledge graph from the corpus (entities and relations) and retrieves with personalised PageRank from query entities. Gives one-step multi-hop retrieval, borrowing the idea of hippocampal indexing.
numbers: Recall@5 on 2WikiMultiHopQA 89.5 (HippoRAG Contriever) vs 68.2 best ColBERTv2; MuSiQue R@5 52.1 vs 49.2; HotpotQA R@5 76.2-77.7 vs 79.3 (not better). Average R@5 72.9 vs 65.6. Cost: 10-30 times cheaper and 6-13 times faster than iterative IRCoT retrieval.
limits: Gain is large on path-finding questions, absent on HotpotQA (weaker multi-hop test). Depends on open IE quality.
agent_relevance: Graph-based retrieval with PageRank is a direct memory design for analogue retrieval across linked concepts. It is code-run, cheap, and testable.

source: Edge, Trinh, Cheng, et al. (2024) From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
finding: LLM builds an entity graph from text, detects communities, writes community summaries, and answers global questions by summarising the partial answers. Beats plain vector RAG on whole-corpus questions.
numbers: Comprehensiveness win rate vs naive RAG 72-83% (p<.001) on podcast transcripts, 72-80% on news; diversity win rate 75-82% and 62-71% respectively; corpora about 1 million tokens. Judged by an LLM; claim-based checks added.
limits: LLM-judged win rates; naive RAG weak on global questions by design; high indexing cost.
agent_relevance: For 'what are the main themes' style memory queries, a community-summary layer helps; for local fact lookup it is not needed.

source: Xu, Mei, Gao, et al. (2025) A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: Zettelkasten-style memory: each memory is a note with keywords and tags; the model links new notes to old ones and updates old notes. A knowledge network inside an agent loop.
numbers: On LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini, A-Mem F1 row reads 27.02 / 45.85 / 16.47 / 44.65 / 50.03 (category columns as printed; header alignment unclear) against MemGPT 26.65 / 25.52 / 12.14 / 41.04 / 43.29. Tokens per answer: 643 (A-Mem) vs 16,910 (MemGPT, LoCoMo). Authors state 85-93% token cut, about 1,200 tokens per memory operation; multi-hop at least 2x baselines on some models.
limits: Author benchmark; baselines win some categories (e.g. LoCoMo single-hop F1 61.56 beats A-Mem 48.43 in one model row); table columns hard to parse from text extraction.
agent_relevance: Links between memory notes can raise multi-hop recall and cut tokens, but link creation is model-judged and adds noise; check with code-side counts.

source: Luo, Chen, Hao, et al. (2024) Large language models surpass human experts in predicting neuroscience results (BrainBench, Nature Human Behaviour 2025)
finding: Models given two versions of an abstract (real result vs altered) pick the real one better than neuroscientists. Shows models absorb the link structure of a literature.
numbers: LLMs mean 81.4% accuracy vs human experts 63.4% (top-20% expertise subset 66.2%); 171 of 202 participants kept. Fine-tuning Mistral-7B on 1.3 billion neuroscience tokens added about 3% on BrainBench.
limits: Forward-looking test of plausibility, not novel discovery; possible contamination not fully ruled out.
agent_relevance: Models carry a latent knowledge network; scoring candidate links by model likelihood is a cheap plausibility filter, to be checked against ground truth.

source: Ghafarollahi & Buehler (2024) SciAgents: Automating scientific discovery through multi-agent intelligent graph reasoning
finding: Random paths through a large ontological knowledge graph of bio-inspired materials seed multi-agent hypothesis writing and critique.
numbers: Case studies only; no controlled comparison or accuracy figure in the paper text I read.
limits: No baseline, no expert blind rating, demonstrations only.
agent_relevance: Path sampling in a graph as the source of cross-domain prompts is a cheap operator; evidence of benefit is anecdotal.

source: Gu & Krenn (2026) SciMuse method
finding: Pipeline: build graph of concepts (billion-edge scale, multi-edges), pick concept pairs near the researcher, give the LLM recent paper titles and abstracts, then self-critique and revise.
numbers: Prompt used up to 7 recent publications per researcher; prompt variants tried in pilots did not improve interest ratings.
limits: Prompt engineering gains were nil in pilots.
agent_relevance: Spending effort on wording the idea prompt gave no measured gain here; spend it on selection and checking.

source: Krenn & Zeilinger (2020) SEMNET growth
finding: Concept links in quantum physics grow unevenly; new concepts such as qubit (1995) and graphene (2005) show emergence of subfields. Example pair 'interaction-free measurement' and 'Leggett-Garg inequality' unlinked in 2012 were linked in a 2014 paper that gained about 100 citations in four years.
numbers: Pair had 60 and 33 abstracts, 135 and 141 neighbours, distance 2, cosine 0.228 (22.8% shared neighbours).
limits: One anecdote chosen at random from unlinked pairs.
agent_relevance: Distance-2 pairs with partial overlap are the sweet spot for new links; usable as a retrieval prior.

source: Krenn et al. (2023) Science4Cast methods ranking
finding: Winning solutions blend gradient boosting (LightGBM) with graph neural nets and features like PageRank and Jaccard index; adding data augmentation raised test AUC by about 0.02 across models. Learned 128-dim node embeddings alone did not reach top.
numbers: AUC up to 0.93 task (delta=3 years, c=0, w=1); +0.02 from augmentation; models with AUC below 0.6 omitted from figure.
limits: Competition split; 2014-2021 data only.
agent_relevance: Pure embeddings lose to engineered features on link prediction; useful caution for vector-only retrieval of analogues.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) failure of LLM self-judgement
finding: LLM ranker separated top and bottom ICLR papers with moderate accuracy; authors report failures of LLM self-evaluation of ideas.
numbers: Ranker pairwise accuracy 71.4% (Claude-3.5-Sonnet); the paper also lists 61.1% and 63.5% (Claude-3-Opus) for other rankers on ICLR accept/reject pairs.
limits: Proxy task (accept/reject), not idea quality.
agent_relevance: Supports schema rule: the model fills slots, code decides. Use pairwise ranking with external ground truth, not self-scoring.

source: Gutierrez et al. (2024) HippoRAG baselines
finding: Structure-augmented baselines such as RAPTOR (tree of summaries) and propositions did not beat a plain ColBERTv2 retriever on average; a graph with PageRank did.
numbers: Average R@5: RAPTOR 56.8 (62.3 with ColBERTv2), Proposition 61.2 (64.4), ColBERTv2 65.6, HippoRAG 72.6-72.9.
limits: Three datasets; one corpus size.
agent_relevance: Not all added structure helps; test each memory structure against the plain retriever.

source: Edge et al. (2024) GraphRAG claim-based check
finding: Global graph-based answers beat vector RAG in comprehensiveness and diversity but not in directness; the trade-off is built in. Text summarisation of everything (no graph) was close behind graph community levels.
numbers: All GraphRAG conditions beat naive RAG on comprehensiveness and diversity; C1-C3 only slightly better than global text summarisation; root-level summaries cheapest and weakest.
limits: Slight gains over simple summarisation; costs not equal.
agent_relevance: The graph is helping, but a plain summary of the whole is a strong comparator; include it in tests.

source: Wang et al. (2023) SciMON retrieval inspirations
finding: Three retrieval sources for inspiration: semantic neighbours (SentenceBERT), knowledge-graph neighbours, citation neighbours. Adding KG context improved some model results; GPT-4 few-shot with KG was equal or slightly preferred in human study.
numbers: GPT4FS+KG preferred in 52%/55% of comparisons on two criteria; most others ties.
limits: Small human studies; ties dominate.
agent_relevance: Graph context helps a little at best; most gain comes from iteration against prior work.

source: Si et al. (2024) diversity limit of idea generation
finding: Repeated sampling hits a ceiling: non-duplicate ideas plateau as more seeds are generated.
numbers: Of 4,000 generated seeds only 200 unique at similarity threshold 0.8.
limits: Single task domain.
agent_relevance: Add a code-side duplication counter and stop when new unique ideas fall off.

source: Luo et al. (2024) BrainBench model size
finding: Small 7B models (Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B) performed comparably to larger ones on the prediction task.
numbers: Exact deltas only in Fig 3A.
limits: Delta values only in figure.
agent_relevance: For latent-knowledge probing, base-style scoring may beat chat prompting.

source: Sourati & Evans (2023) people matter in network
finding: Authors-aware random walks: of trial-cited papers, 75% appear in the walks; 40% of top 50 ranked potential authors became actual discoverers within a year for thermoelectric and ferroelectric materials.
numbers: 75% of trial-cited papers (five years before) and 60% of their authors were sampled by the walk; 40% of top-50 ranked authors became discoverers within a year for thermoelectric and ferroelectric materials, 20% for another property.
limits: Retrospective; materials and drugs only.
agent_relevance: Modelling the source of a claim, not just its content, adds predictive power; useful for provenance tags in memory.

source: Gu & Krenn (2026) SciMuse limits on humans
finding: Authors note ideas that are interesting must balance novelty and nearness: too obscure, too obvious, unfeasible or unexciting all lower ratings. Graph control of properties works even when the quality does not rise.
numbers: Mean 2.40 on 5-point scale; response count fell later in the questionnaire but mean rating stayed steady (no order effect shown).
limits: Self-reported by authors; one institution.
agent_relevance: Use graph features as controls (distance, degree) rather than as quality predictors.
